The master of the Ice Wheel Palace gave the boy a new name, like all his senior brothers—a name of the moon: Crimson Wheel. 
The moon is the essential foundation for all who practice cultivation in this world, and the core of the Ice Wheel Palace's teachings. 
The silent Crimson Wheel was obedient, diligent, and earnest. By day, he studied pharmacology intently in the alchemy room; by night, he gazed at the bright moon from the courtyard, lost in thought. 
Within the vast ocean of scriptures, Crimson Wheel discovered a legend from a mysterious western land: using a special art, one could scoop the moon from water and obtain a rare, potent medicine. 
Medicine. Crimson Wheel's fingers trembled as they traced the characters. If he had been faster, earlier back then... could he have found the formula to save his parents? 
Crimson Wheel tried every art he has learned—by the alchemy pool, by the river, at the clear spring... but he could never lift the moon from the water. 
His senior brothers laughed at his foolishness. Yet he only repeated the gestures toward the moon's reflection, trying again and again to scoop it up. 
Finally, he bid his master farewell and once more set out on his journey to find the medicine.

It is said that those who shared a boat in past lives now share a pillow in this one.
Who would have thought that Shangguan would encounter Liu Si'an?
A day as husband and wife brings the wish to grow old together; a hundred days of affection forge the bond of holding hands.
Shangguan and Anniang once dreamed of witnessing Chang'an's splendor, singing under the moon.
Their union drew envy, and their love brought joy to Heaven and Earth.
Yet time sowed discord, fate bound them, hardships arose, and grievances festered.
Anniang, gentle as willow, kind and meek, could neither serve her in-laws nor manage the household.
Now, releasing Anniang brings relief. May she find another Uncommon home.
May she drink beneath blossoms, gaze at the moon, and be blessed with grandchildren. May her clan rejoice, and Shangguan have no regrets.
As proof, in Chang'an's Wannian County,
Shangguan Ze solemnly writes.
